title: Deletions making a search tree degenerate
summary: Repeatedly deleting nodes from one side of a binary search tree without rebalancing can push the subtree height difference beyond the balance limit and leave a one-sided chain.
context: A node's balance factor is its left subtree height minus its right subtree height, with leaf height 0 and empty subtree height −1; a tree is balanced only when every node's balance factor has absolute value at most 1. The balance factors below are computed from the connections shown.

Across the three subfigures, nodes 5 and 3 are deleted in turn, reducing the node count from 5 to 4 and then to 3 under the labels "Balanced binary tree", "Ordinary binary tree", and "Linked list"; no rotational rebalancing is performed.
result: Value ordering still holds, but the tree has degenerated into a chain. An AVL tree must maintain balance after deletions.

frames.title: Deletions making a search tree degenerate
frames.explanation: Initially, root 4 has left and right children 2 and 5, and 2 has left and right children 1 and 3. Deleting right leaf node 5 leaves root 4 with left subtree height 1 and an empty right subtree of height −1, so its balance factor becomes 1 − (−1) = 2 and the tree is already unbalanced. Deleting right leaf node 3 of node 2 next leaves only the all-left chain 4 → 2 → 1.

steps.title: Initial balanced tree
steps.explanation: Initially, root 4 connects to left 2 and right 5, and 2 connects to left 1 and right 3; 1, 3, and 5 are leaf nodes, for 5 nodes in total. The root's left and right subtrees have heights 1 and 0, giving balance factor 1, while every other node has balance factor 0, so the whole tree is balanced.
steps.key_state: Initial root 4 connects to left 2 and right 5, and 2 connects to left 1 and right 3; 5 nodes in total, with root balance factor 1.
steps.announcement: Show the initial balanced binary search tree with 5 nodes.

steps.title: Delete right leaf node 5
steps.explanation: After deleting right leaf node 5, root 4 has only left child 2, while 2 still connects to left 1 and right 3, for 4 nodes in total. The root's left subtree has height 1 and its empty right side has height −1, giving balance factor 2, so the tree is already unbalanced.
steps.key_state: After deleting 5, root 4 connects only to left 2, and 2 connects to left 1 and right 3; 4 nodes in total, with root balance factor 2.
steps.announcement: Delete right leaf node 5; root 4's balance factor rises to 2, making the tree unbalanced.

steps.title: Only a left chain remains after deleting node 3
steps.explanation: Deleting right leaf node 3 of node 2 next leaves root 4 connected only to left 2, 2 connected only to left 1, and leaf node 1, forming the 3-node all-left chain 4→2→1.
steps.key_state: After deleting 5 and 3, only the all-left chain 4→2→1 remains, with 3 nodes in total.
steps.announcement: Delete leaf node 3 as well; the remaining nodes form the all-left chain 4 → 2 → 1.
